originality.rationale: The general maximal-independent-set count distributions in Drmota et al. do not imply membership-query VC/Littlestone dimensions; the Guingona et al. exact equality theorem concerns zero-sets of linear combinations, not maximal independent sets; Michel-Scott use maximal-independent-set outputs as an oracle to reconstruct an unknown graph, reversing the known/hidden objects. No inspected claim or indexed research record implies the unique first eight-vertex adaptive gap, its actual complete decision tree, or the unbounded repeated-copy difference. Risk remains for unindexed historical work.
residual_risks: Indexed and full-text literature cannot prove absolute historical priority; earlier unindexed, differently phrased, or inaccessible work could contain a matching classification.

The result does not assert uniqueness or extremality for connected trees of order greater than eight.

value.rationale: The natural learning problem is to predict membership in an unknown maximal independent set of a known tree. The first order at which adaptive shattering strictly outperforms fixed-support shattering, and the unique extremal shape, are structurally motivated finite invariants. A complete finite classification plus an explicit adaptive witness is not a textbook deduction from MIS counts; disjoint-copy additivity then makes the gap unbounded over acyclic graphs, identifying a genuine qualitative difference.
